categories.main_business_segments: Curtiss-Wright operates through three reportable segments: Aerospace & Industrial, Defense Electronics, and Naval & Power. The Aerospace & Industrial segment serves commercial aerospace and general industrial markets. Defense Electronics focuses on defense and, to a lesser extent, commercial aerospace markets. Naval & Power primarily serves naval defense and power & process markets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in highly engineered products and solutions, including electronic throttle controls, sensors, actuation components, embedded computing modules, tactical communications, naval propulsion equipment, and advanced valve technologies. Manufacturing processes involve material modification, precision machining, assembly, and rigorous testing, with both commercial-grade and ruggedized, military-grade production standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Curtiss-Wright's key customers include agencies and prime contractors of the U.S. Government (notably the Department of Defense and U.S. Navy), commercial aerospace OEMs (such as Boeing and Airbus), nuclear power plant operators, and industrial OEMs in sectors like transportation, oil & gas, and general industry. The company serves aerospace defense, ground defense, naval defense, commercial aerospace, power & process, and general industrial markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with principal manufacturing facilities in the U.S. (Arizona, California, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina), Canada, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. In 2021, 26% of sales were to customers outside the U.S., with significant operations and sales in Europe, Canada, China, and other international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Curtiss-Wright primarily operates as an OEM and tier-one/tier-two supplier, providing mission-critical components, subsystems, and services to both upstream (defense and aerospace primes) and downstream (industrial and power plant operators) customers. The company is positioned midstream in the supply chain, integrating advanced technologies into customer platforms.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include consistent growth in sales and margins, disciplined capital deployment (including acquisitions), and reinvestment in innovation. R&D focuses on emerging defense technologies (C4ISR, cyber, hypersonics, MOSA), electrification, digitalization for nuclear power, and advanced industrial automation. The company emphasizes engineering leadership and expanding its portfolio in high-growth, mission-critical applications.
categories.revenue_model: Curtiss-Wright generates revenue primarily through product sales (both standard and custom-engineered), long-term contracts, and aftermarket services such as maintenance, repair, and overhaul. Approximately half of revenue is recognized over time (long-term contracts), with the remainder at point-of-sale. Service sales and recurring aftermarket support are significant in certain segments.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes with larger, well-capitalized firms in defense, aerospace, and industrial markets, as well as specialized niche players. It is positioned as a market leader or significant player in several niche markets due to its engineering expertise, technological innovation, and strong customer relationships. Competition is based on technology, quality, performance, price, and customer service.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, Curtiss-Wright reported $2.5 billion in sales, a 5% increase over 2020, with operating income of $383 million (32% growth). The company has a global workforce of approximately 7,800 employees and a market capitalization of $4.8 billion as of mid-2021. Growth is driven by defense and industrial markets, with a strong backlog ($2.2 billion) and a focus on both organic and acquisition-led expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Curtiss-Wright delivers highly engineered, mission-critical products and solutions that improve safety, efficiency, and reliability in demanding environments. Its differentiation lies in technical sophistication, decades of engineering expertise, and the ability to provide niche, cost-effective solutions for critical applications. The company emphasizes quality, innovation, and customer-centric customization as key value drivers.
